summary: Worse than national: the killing of the territory's most publicly visible trans person, followed by a refusal to investigate. On 8 August 2024 a 33-year-old transgender woman with a large TikTok following ('Abuja Area Mama') was found beaten and bruised beside the Katampe-Mabushi Expressway hours after posting a routine video, having previously expressed fear for her life; a human-rights group has since sued the federal government and the police for failing to investigate, seeking a court order compelling investigation and prosecution after multiple petitions were ignored — which qualifies the killing under the state-failure test rather than leaving it a lone incident. Reporting on the capital's queer scene documents threats and raids alongside informal community organising. The national framework applies here unchanged: same-sex conduct criminalised with up to 14 years' imprisonment, with dating-app 'kito' gangs a nationwide pattern; the UK's foreign office warned LGBT travellers in August 2026 of arrest, violence, attacks and blackmail risks. Scored relative to the national score (0.08) for Nigeria.

sources.summary: BBC News (9 August 2024): Nigerian transgender TikToker 'Abuja Area Mama' found dead — the beaten and bruised body of the 33-year-old transgender woman was found along a highway in the capital, Abuja; she had expressed fears for her life the previous year; police are investigating.

The Dial, 'Threats, Raids and Potlucks' (issue 25): feature reporting on the queer scene in the capital alongside the 'Abuja Area Mama' case, documenting the surrounding climate of threats and raids and informal community organising.

Sahara Reporters (19 August 2026): the UK foreign office's latest travel advice warns LGBT+ travellers to Nigeria of arrest, violence, attacks, blackmail and intimidation — same-sex sexual activity illegal, up to 14 years' imprisonment, and death-penalty risks under religious law in the northern states.
